assessment: Pixel review supports KILL as a background/correction artifact. Primary-event difference images in sectors 69, 103 and 104 are dominated by diffuse changes across the cutout; sector 96 has weak structure near the target, without a consistent point source across sectors. The fixed, sky-subtracted target aperture gives brightening in sectors 69 and 103 (-82.209 +/- 2.104 and -3.273 +/- 0.562 ppt), a weak 1.266 +/- 0.533-ppt dip in sector 96, and an unstable 8.857 +/- 3.257-ppt change in sector 104 [M]. Large raw-aperture and sky ramps closely track one another; gap-adjacent excursions and broad steps do not reproduce a stable, localized transit at the accepted ephemeris. These pixel measurements do not support the fitted 3.926-ppt maximum dip. The verdict is based on instrumental evidence; astrophysical FPP does not include these instrumental hypotheses.
what_would_change: To reconsider: independent photometry must reproduce repeated dimming localized to a stellar source with stable background, including a consistent depth and transit shape across sectors. The fixed-box errors describe local point scatter and omit some correlated noise.
scope: Final local pixel assessment, retained after the main coordinator completed C and refreshed all six Stage D catalogues. No external submission was made.

figures.caption: Primary and phase-0.5 difference images at the accepted physical-fit ephemeris; Gaia positions are propagated to each sector epoch.

Fixed target aperture and sky variations, full phase and transit windows after sky subtraction. All four sectors use the same aperture and background geometry with a 300-arcsec Gaia cone covering the target aperture and background annulus.

background_mask_review.scope: Supplied Gaia sources on the cutout use the same fixed mask geometry. The 300-arcsec cone covers the target aperture and the background annulus, including the two-pixel source-exclusion margin; full corner coverage of a 21-by-21-pixel square is not required for that annulus.
background_mask_review.outcome: Both diagnostic figures and the packet summary inspected. No aperture, ephemeris, detrending or science gate was tuned.
